title: Reference-Guided Turn-Taking Style Transfer for Full-Duplex Spoken Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.20763v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Full-duplex spoken language models decide at every frame whether to take the floor, defining a conversational personality -- yet each set of weights encodes exactly one, which human speakers bracket rather than share. Existing controls mostly act from outside; none identifies the quantity that sets how much the model speaks. We identify it: a single late-layer residual-stream direction, the initiative vector, extracted from the model's own conversations without training or annotation. The same direction reads the decision, anticipating onsets up to 800 ms ahead, and shifts it: scaled during generation, it moves speech ratio from 6-12% to 42-61% (no steering: 21-30%), consistently across conversations, weights, and corpora. A short reference recording suffices to transfer a speaker's turn-taking style to the model, and the transfer is reference-specific: swapping in another speaker's reference worsens the match in 93-98% of cases, where

translated_title: 面向全双工口语模型的参考引导话轮转换风格迁移
translated_abstract: 全双工口语语言模型在每一帧都要决定是否“接过话轮”，这一决策定义了一种对话个性——然而每一组模型权重只编码了唯一一种个性，而人类说话者是在不同个性之间灵活切换而非固守单一一种。现有的控制手段大多从模型外部施加作用；没有任何方法识别出决定模型说话量的那个内在量。我们识别出了这个量：一个单一的深层残差流方向——“主动性向量”，它可以从模型自身的对话中提取，无需任何训练或标注。同一个方向既能读取话轮决策，可提前至多800毫秒预判发言开始；又能改变这一决策：在生成过程中对其进行缩放，可将模型说话比例从6-12%提升至42-61%（无干预时为21-30%），且在不同对话、不同权重和不同语料库上均保持一致。一段简短的参考录音就足以将该说话者的话轮转换风格迁移给模型，且这种迁移具有参考对象特异性：换用另一位说话者的参考录音，会在93-98%的情况下使风格匹配效果变差。
tldr: 本文识别出决定全双工口语模型说话量的内在量——一个无需训练或标注即可从模型自身对话中提取的深层残差流方向“主动性向量”，它既能提前800毫秒预测话轮决策，又能通过缩放干预将模型说话比例从6-12%调控至42-61%，并仅凭一段简短参考录音即可实现针对特定说话者的话轮风格迁移。
en_tdlr: The paper identifies a single late-layer residual-stream direction—the "initiative vector," extracted from a model's own conversations without training or annotation—as the quantity governing how much a full-duplex spoken language model speaks, enabling turn-decision prediction up to 800 ms in advance, steering of speech ratio from 6-12% to 42-61%, and reference-specific transfer of a speaker's turn-taking style from a short recording.
